plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 4: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
plan.contextChunk: This figure places two orbital-overlap drawings side by side to contrast the bonding geometry of an open chain with that of a three-membered ring. On the left, three carbons lettered "C" sit at the ends and apex of a shallow V, with black dashed lines drawn through them marking the straight paths from nucleus to nucleus. Pink lobes of electron density project from each carbon along those dashed lines and meet head-on midway between neighboring atoms, the overlap regions shaded a deeper rose. A magenta double-headed arc spans the angle at the central carbon, labeled "109°". On the right, three carbons lettered "C" occupy the corners of a triangle. Dashed lines again mark the internuclear directions, but the pink lobes now emerge tilted away from them, so each pair meets outside the edge of the triangle rather than along the line joining the two carbons, leaving the interior open. Bold captions read "Typical alkane C−C bonds" and "Typical bent cyclopropane C−C bonds". Drawing the internuclear lines in both panels lets the reader compare where the lobes point against where the atoms actually lie, which accounts for why a ring squeezed to a 60 degree angle forms curved, poorly overlapped bonds that are weaker and more reactive than ordinary ones.

elements: Left panel: three carbon nuclei drawn as bold letter 'C' — one apex carbon at top center, two terminal carbons lower-left and lower-right, forming a shallow wide V
Left panel: black dashed internuclear lines drawn through apex C to each terminal C, extended a short distance beyond every nucleus
Left panel: two large pink sp3 hybrid lobes on the apex carbon, aimed directly down the two dashed lines
Left panel: one large pink sp3 lobe on each terminal carbon, aimed back up its dashed line toward the apex
Left panel: deeper rose head-on overlap patch centered on each dashed line midway between bonded carbons
Left panel: magenta double-headed curved arc spanning the C–C–C angle below the atoms
Left panel: magenta '109°' text label inside the arc
Right panel: three carbon nuclei lettered 'C' at the corners of an upright triangle (apex top center, two base carbons lower-left and lower-right)
Right panel: black dashed lines marking the three internuclear directions (triangle edges), extended beyond the nuclei; includes a near-vertical dashed line through the apex and lower-left carbon
Right panel: six pink sp3 lobes, two per carbon, each tilted outward away from its internuclear dashed line
Right panel: three banana-shaped overlap regions sitting outside each triangle edge, leaving the triangle interior empty
Bold caption 'Typical alkane C−C bonds' beneath left panel
Bold caption 'Typical bent cyclopropane C−C bonds' beneath right panel
Radial pink-to-rose shading inside each lobe giving 3D teardrop appearance

interactions.teaches: Head-on overlap along the internuclear axis in an open chain versus off-axis 'banana' overlap forced by a three-membered ring; the dashed nucleus-to-nucleus guides stay drawn in both so the learner can see where the lobes point relative to where the atoms actually are
interactions.label: Bonding geometry

interactions.teaches: Squeezing the C−C−C angle from 109° toward 60° cannot drag the sp3 orbitals with it: the lobes stay near their preferred ~104° separation, so they bend away from the dashed internuclear lines, the overlap patch slides outward off the line, and overlap quality drops — the origin of cyclopropane's strained, curved, reactive bonds
interactions.label: C−C−C internuclear angle

interactions.teaches: Isolating the deep-rose overlap patch makes visible how much lobe density actually shares space, and how that shared region migrates outside the internuclear line as the angle closes
interactions.label: Highlight overlap region

demo_steps.title: Normal tetrahedral bonding
demo_steps.narration: At 109° the sp3 lobes lie right on the black dashed internuclear lines and meet head-on midway between nuclei — maximum, symmetric overlap and a strong ordinary C−C bond.

demo_steps.title: Compressing the angle
demo_steps.narration: Drag the angle down toward 90°. The nuclei move closer together but the lobes resist following, so each orbital axis now sits several degrees off its dashed line and the rose overlap patch begins to slip outward.

demo_steps.title: Forced to 60°
demo_steps.narration: At 60° each orbital misses its internuclear line by roughly 22°. Overlap is small and lies outside the line joining the nuclei — this is a bent, poorly overlapped bond.

demo_steps.title: Cyclopropane's banana bonds
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the ring: three 60° angles give six outward-tilted lobes whose overlap bulges outside each triangle edge, leaving the interior empty. The same dashed triangle shows how far the bonds curve from the straight nucleus-to-nucleus paths.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Flat front-on layout in the XY plane, +X screen-right, +Y screen-up; lobes are solids of revolution so they read as 3D teardrops but the pose is front-on. ALKANE PANEL (default view): apex carbon at (0, 0.9); C−C distance 2.4 world units; terminal carbons placed at apex + 2.4·(cos, sin) of half-angle each side, i.e. at 109° opening they sit near (-1.96, -0.51) and (+1.96, -0.51) — a shallow wide V opening downward, apex on top. Dashed black (#1A1A1A, dash 0.12/0.10, width ~0.02) lines run through apex to each terminal C and extend ~0.6 units past every nucleus. Bold serif 'C' labels sit ON each nucleus with a small white halo so dashes pass behind them. Each sp3 lobe: teardrop ~1.5 units long, max radius ~0.55, narrow end anchored at the nucleus, fat end toward the bond midpoint; apex carbon carries two lobes, each terminal carbon one lobe pointing back at the apex. Overlap patch = deeper rose lens where the two lobes interpenetrate, centered on the bond midpoint when angle = 109°. Magenta arc (#E5127D, width 0.03, double arrowheads) spans below the terminal carbons from left dashed line to right dashed line, sagging ~0.8 units below the V, with '109°' in matching magenta at its center; arc label text updates with the slider. CYCLOPROPANE PANEL: equilateral triangle, side 2.4, apex carbon at (0, 1.4), base carbons at (-1.2, -0.68) and (+1.2, -0.68); dashed lines along all three edges extended ~0.8 past each vertex (the apex-to-lower-left edge reads as the near-vertical dashed line in the source). Each carbon carries two lobes, one per bond, each rotated OUTWARD from the ring center by 22° off its internuclear line; overlap lenses therefore sit ~0.45 units outside each edge midpoint, ring interior left empty. BEND FORMULA: interorbital angle held at a constant ~104°; bend of each lobe off its internuclear line = (104° − currentCCCangle)/2, i.e. 0° at ~104–109°, 7° at 90°, 22° at 60°; overlap-patch outward offset ≈ 1.2·sin(bend). PALETTE: lobe outer haze soft pink #F2A6B6 at ~35% opacity, lobe body #E4839A, deep overlap core rose #B5486A / #9C3A5C, internal highlight streak near-white #FBE3E9; dashed lines #1A1A1A; angle arc and degree label magenta #E5127D; captions bold black #000000 on white #FFFFFF background.
interactionPlan.notes: Render lobes as LatheGeometry teardrop profiles (radius r(t) = 0.55·sin(πt)^0.8 · t^0.3 along axis length 1.5) with MeshBasicMaterial + additive-ish layered transparency, or as billboarded sprites with a radial gradient texture to reproduce the airbrushed pink shading; two nested shells (wide translucent haze + tighter opaque core) reproduce the source's soft edge. Overlap patch: draw a separate lens mesh at the intersection with darker rose and higher opacity, toggled by showOverlap; compute its center analytically from the two lobe axes rather than by CSG. Disable depth-write on translucent lobes and sort back-to-front to avoid seams. Dashed lines via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(); 'C' labels and captions as HTML/CSS overlay or CanvasTexture sprites that stay screen-facing and non-scaling. The 109° arc is a CircleGeometry arc strip plus two small cone arrowheads. On slider change, rebuild nuclei positions and re-aim lobe quaternions each frame (cheap: 6 meshes max); tween panelToggle transitions over ~500 ms by morphing nucleus positions so the V visibly closes into the triangle. Orthographic-style framing: fixed front-on camera, figure spans ~7 world units wide, no user rotation.

authoredContext:
How can the hybrid-orbital model of bonding account for the large distortion of bond angles from the normal 109° tetrahedral value to 60° in cyclopropane? The answer is that cyclopropane has bent bonds. In an unstrained alkane, maximum bonding is achieved when two atoms have their overlapping orbitals pointing directly toward each other. In cyclopropane, though, the orbitals can’t point directly toward each other; instead, they overlap at a slight angle. The result is that cyclopropane bonds are weaker and more reactive than typical alkane bonds—255 kJ/mol (61 kcal/mol) for a C−C bond in cyclopropane versus 370 kJ/mol (88 kcal/mol) for a C−C bond in open-chain propane.

Orbital representations show typical alkane C-C bonds with 109 degrees angle and typical bent cyclopropane C-C bonds.

discrepancies: The magenta 109° arc is drawn at a much larger radius than in the source — it sweeps far below the terminal carbons leaving a large empty gap, whereas in the source it hugs just beneath the two C atoms.
The '109°' text sits well above the arc in open space rather than being nestled inside/along the arc as in the source, so it reads as detached from the annotation it belongs to.

The sp³ lobes render as elongated, fused pink smears along each bond axis; the source shows four distinct fat teardrop lobes (two per bond) with clearly visible individual outlines and a bright overlap lens between them.

The dashed internuclear lines extend only a short stub past each terminal C, and the apex lobes are pinched very thin near the central carbon, making the lobe-on-line relationship less obvious than in the source.
The caption sits much farther below the figure than in the source, leaving an unusually large vertical gap and off-centre composition.
evaluation.notes: Recognizable, correctly coloured reproduction of the alkane panel with a toggle to the cyclopropane panel and a rich, conceptually apt set of interactions (angle slider, overlap toggle, guided steps, hover tooltips); main weaknesses are the oversized/mis-placed 109° arc and label and lobes that read as fused smears rather than the distinct teardrops of the source.
action_items: Shrink the angle arc radius (~1.3–1.6× bond length instead of 2.85) so it passes just below the terminal C labels, and place the '109°' label on/inside the arc midpoint as in the source.

Increase lobe width and reduce shell elongation/opacity blending so each of the four sp³ lobes reads as a distinct teardrop with a visible overlap lens, rather than a continuous pink smear along the bond.
Extend the dashed internuclear lines further past the terminal carbons (source shows generous overshoot) and keep the apex ends of lobes fuller so the lobe/line relationship is visible.
Tighten vertical layout: move the caption closer under the arc so the composition matches the source's compact framing.
plan_action_items: Consider showing both panels side by side by default (as in the source two-panel figure) with the toggle used only to zoom/emphasise, so the alkane-vs-cyclopropane comparison is visible at a glance.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; the issues are concrete rendering details (arc radius/label placement, lobe shape and opacity, dashed line extents, caption spacing) that belong to the generator.

ALKANE PANEL (default view): apex carbon at (0, 0.9); C−C distance 2.4 world units; terminal carbons placed at apex + 2.4·(cos, sin) of half-angle each side, i.e. at 109° opening they sit near (-1.96, -0.51) and (+1.96, -0.51) — a shallow wide V opening downward, apex on top. Dashed black (#1A1A1A, dash 0.12/0.10, width ~0.02) lines run through apex to each terminal C and extend ~0.6 units past every nucleus. Bold serif 'C' labels sit ON each nucleus with a small white halo so dashes pass behind them. Each sp3 lobe: teardrop ~1.5 units long, max radius ~0.55, narrow end anchored at the nucleus, fat end toward the bond midpoint; apex carbon carries two lobes, each terminal carbon one lobe pointing back at the apex. Overlap patch = deeper rose lens where the two lobes interpenetrate, centered on the bond midpoint when angle = 109°. Magenta arc (#E5127D, width 0.03, double arrowheads) spans below the terminal carbons from left dashed line to right dashed line, sagging ~0.8 units below the V, with '109°' in matching magenta at its center; arc label text updates with the slider. CYCLOPROPANE PANEL: equilateral triangle, side 2.4, apex carbon at (0, 1.4), base carbons at (-1.2, -0.68) and (+1.2, -0.68); dashed lines along all three edges extended ~0.8 past each vertex (the apex-to-lower-left edge reads as the near-vertical dashed line in the source). Each carbon carries two lobes, one per bond, each rotated OUTWARD from the ring center by 22° off its internuclear line; overlap lenses therefore sit ~0.45 units outside each edge midpoint, ring interior left empty. BEND FORMULA: interorbital angle held at a constant ~104°; bend of each lobe off its internuclear line = (104° − currentCCCangle)/2, i.e. 0° at ~104–109°, 7° at 90°, 22° at 60°; overlap-patch outward offset ≈ 1.2·sin(bend). PALETTE: lobe outer haze soft pink #F2A6B6 at ~35% opacity, lobe body #E4839A, deep overlap core rose #B5486A / #9C3A5C, internal highlight streak near-white #FBE3E9; dashed lines #1A1A1A; angle arc and degree label magenta #E5127D; captions bold black #000000 on white #FFFFFF background.
interactionPlan.notes: Render lobes as LatheGeometry teardrop profiles (radius r(t) = 0.55·sin(πt)^0.8 · t^0.3 along axis length 1.5) with MeshBasicMaterial + additive-ish layered transparency, or as billboarded sprites with a radial gradient texture to reproduce the airbrushed pink shading; two nested shells (wide translucent haze + tighter opaque core) reproduce the source's soft edge. Overlap patch: draw a separate lens mesh at the intersection with darker rose and higher opacity, toggled by showOverlap; compute its center analytically from the two lobe axes rather than by CSG. Disable depth-write on translucent lobes and sort back-to-front to avoid seams. Dashed lines via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(); 'C' labels and captions as HTML/CSS overlay or CanvasTexture sprites that stay screen-facing and non-scaling. The 109° arc is a CircleGeometry arc strip plus two small cone arrowheads. On slider change, rebuild nuclei positions and re-aim lobe quaternions each frame (cheap: 6 meshes max); tween panelToggle transitions over ~500 ms by morphing nucleus positions so the V visibly closes into the triangle. Orthographic-style framing: fixed front-on camera, figure spans ~7 world units wide, no user rotation.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure places two orbital-overlap drawings side by side to contrast the bonding geometry of an open chain with that of a three-membered ring. On the left, three carbons lettered "C" sit at the ends and apex of a shallow V, with black dashed lines drawn through them marking the straight paths from nucleus to nucleus. Pink lobes of electron density project from each carbon along those dashed lines and meet head-on midway between neighboring atoms, the overlap regions shaded a deeper rose. A magenta double-headed arc spans the angle at the central carbon, labeled "109°". On the right, three carbons lettered "C" occupy the corners of a triangle. Dashed lines again mark the internuclear directions, but the pink lobes now emerge tilted away from them, so each pair meets outside the edge of the triangle rather than along the line joining the two carbons, leaving the interior open. Bold captions read "Typical alkane C−C bonds" and "Typical bent cyclopropane C−C bonds". Drawing the internuclear lines in both panels lets the reader compare where the lobes point against where the atoms actually lie, which accounts for why a ring squeezed to a 60 degree angle forms curved, poorly overlapped bonds that are weaker and more reactive than ordinary ones.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for decreasing the C-C-C angle from a typical alkane value toward 60 degrees; the pink orbital lobes bend away from the dashed internuclear lines and the overlap patch shifts outward, showing why cyclopropane bonds are curved and strained.
- Toggle between Typical alkane C-C bonds and Typical bent cyclopropane C-C bonds; the same dashed nucleus-to-nucleus guides remain visible, making head-on overlap versus off-axis overlap the comparison to track.

Bonding geometry
Guided walk-through

discrepancies: Lobe rendering differs in character: the source lobes are soft, airbrushed fat teardrops with a smooth gradient, while the generated lobes are built from four nested Lathe shells that read as visible concentric contour rings / banded stripes, giving a 'onion-ring' look rather than a diffuse orbital cloud.

Proportions of the sp³ lobes are off — generated lobes are longer and narrower relative to the C−C distance, so the two bonds merge into one dense dark streak between the carbons; the source keeps each lobe stubby with a clearly visible lens of overlap at the midpoint.

The figure is locked front-on with controls.enableRotate permanently disabled and all materials MeshBasicMaterial with depthTest:false, so there is no occlusion, shading, or depth cue at all — the orbitals read as flat painted shapes rather than volumes (defensible given the flat source, but it removes any 3D affordance).

The magenta 109° arc in the source is a thin sweeping arrow that clearly spans between the two extended dashed lines; the generated arc sags lower and its arrowheads sit slightly detached/rotated relative to the dashed line ends.

The cyclopropane panel is only reachable via the mode toggle (fine), but as built it replaces the alkane rather than sitting beside it, so the side-by-side comparison that is the entire point of the source figure is never seen simultaneously.
evaluation.notes: Composition, colors, dashed internuclear lines, 109° arc and labels closely track the source and the interaction set (mode toggle, angle slider, overlap toggle, guided walk-through, hover explanations) is rich and pedagogically on-point; the main weaknesses are banded/over-elongated orbital lobes that lose the soft airbrushed look of the original and a fully locked front-on view with no depth cues.

feedback.rationale: The concept, elements, and interaction set are correct; the issues are rendering-level (banded lathe shells, lobe proportions, locked camera, arc arrowhead placement, panel layout) that call for implementation fixes rather than a new plan.

demo_steps.title: Normal tetrahedral bonding
demo_steps.narration: At 109° the sp3 lobes lie right on the black dashed internuclear lines and meet head-on midway between nuclei — maximum, symmetric overlap and a strong ordinary C−C bond.

demo_steps.title: Compressing the angle
demo_steps.narration: Drag the angle down toward 90°. The nuclei move closer together but the lobes resist following, so each orbital axis now sits several degrees off its dashed line and the rose overlap patch begins to slip outward.

demo_steps.title: Forced to 60°
demo_steps.narration: At 60° each orbital misses its internuclear line by roughly 22°. Overlap is small and lies outside the line joining the nuclei — this is a bent, poorly overlapped bond.

demo_steps.title: Cyclopropane's banana bonds
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the ring: three 60° angles give six outward-tilted lobes whose overlap bulges outside each triangle edge, leaving the interior empty. The same dashed triangle shows how far the bonds curve from the straight nucleus-to-nucleus paths.

discrepancies: Orbital lobes read as thin, airbrushed smears rather than the fat, well-defined teardrop sp³ lobes of the source; the four individual lobes are no longer distinguishable as separate shapes along each bond.

The source's lens-shaped overlap region where two lobes interpenetrate is replaced by a small circular bright core blob at the middle of each bond, which looks like a nucleus/dot rather than an overlap lens.

Lobe proportions are off: generated lobes are much longer and narrower relative to the C−C distance than the stubby, wide lobes in the source, so the figure looks like two light beams instead of overlapping orbitals.
Overall pink density is far lighter/more washed out than the saturated rose/crimson shading in the source; the dark inner shading of each lobe is missing except at the very centre.

In the source the outer lobes extend visibly past each terminal carbon edge with rounded fat ends; here the density tapers to nothing at the terminal C, weakening the sense of discrete atomic orbitals.
evaluation.notes: Composition, camera, dashed internuclear lines, 109° arc and labels are faithful, and the interaction set (panel toggle, angle slider, overlap toggle, guided steps, hover explanations) is rich and pedagogically apt, but the sp³ lobes render as thin washed-out smears with a circular core instead of the source's fat, saturated teardrops with a lens-shaped overlap, which weakens recognizability.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual decomposition and interaction plan are faithful; the issues are purely rendering details (lobe shape, proportions, saturation, and overlap lens geometry) that should be fixed in the generation implementation.
